# Local WGPU 30 patch

Source: crates.io `wgpu` and `wgpu-core` 30.0.0, with original licenses and source metadata retained. Review the exact changes in [../incular-wgpu.patch](../incular-wgpu.patch).

WGPU forces `wgsl` for native builds because its indirect draw/dispatch validation and timestamp normalization parse internal shaders. Removing that dependency feature alone would make those paths panic. The accompanying wgpu-core patch therefore embeds those same internal shaders as build-time parsed Naga modules, retaining their runtime validation and HAL compilation. Dispatch validation still substitutes the device's actual workgroup limit into the named literal expression. Internal shaders use the same embedded-module path even when `wgsl` is enabled, so the targeted tests exercise the patch.

The public `wgsl` feature continues to enable runtime source parsing for applications that use it. Incular's built-in renderer embeds all 13 of its shaders and does not need that frontend at runtime. All native backends remain enabled. Two warning-only compatibility adjustments gate a now-optional import and change an upstream unused-field lint expectation to an allowance.

This is a maintained dependency patch, not an upstream release. Rebase and review both copies and their shader serialization when updating WGPU/Naga. Build-time and runtime modules must use the same resolved Naga version; generated bytes are never persisted between versions.

Cargo workspace patches do not propagate into independently published application workspaces. Downstream consumers need both patches until upstream supports this path to reproduce this binary-size result. Without the patches the code remains functional, but the forced parser prevents the size saving.
